subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw own a portable cross-backend memory provenance and influence-policy contract, or leave trust enforcement entirely to selected memory plugins and MCP integrations?
rationale: This choice sets a security boundary and compatibility contract across ingestion, storage, promotion, retrieval, compaction, plugins, and persisted state; source inspection cannot determine the intended permanent ownership model.

options.title: Define portable core contract
options.body: Add framework-assigned provenance, review, expiry, and influence fields to the memory host and plugin SDK, then implement the contract in the recommended default backend.

options.title: Plugin and MCP ownership
options.body: Keep core retrieval generic and document maintained integrations such as world-model-mcp as the supported path for trust-governed memory.

options.title: Provenance first
options.body: Land the narrower attribution contract tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42647 before deciding trust scoring and enforcement policy.

recommendation.title: Define portable core contract
recommendation.body: Add framework-assigned provenance, review, expiry, and influence fields to the memory host and plugin SDK, then implement the contract in the recommended default backend.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the prior design review and have the strongest available history signal across the central memory contract files.
